clue.text: Evil doctor to leave car on bend by London landmark

parts.note: Mr Hyde is the evil alter ego of Dr Jekyll in Stevenson's novella
to leave a car somewhere is to park it
a bend in the road is a corner

explanation.surface: A villainous doctor abandons his vehicle on a curve near a famous London sight.
explanation.walkthrough: HYDE PARK CORNER is a busy junction at the south-east corner of Hyde Park in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The junction beside the royal park is a well-known spot in central London, home to Wellington Arch.

clue.text: Soldier returned as in a terrible rush

indicators.note: in places the turned-round word inside the jumbled letters
terrible suggests the word rush is mangled into a new order
returned means the little word as is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone describes coming back in a dreadful hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' reads as an adjective describing the rush, but it signals the anagram; 'in' and 'returned' handle the small word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar is a light cavalryman, a kind of soldier.

clue.text: A name in a recipe from Denmark

indicators.note: in tells us the article and the initial sit inside the dish

parts.note: a recipe makes a dish, so the one stands for the other

explanation.surface: Someone spots a name in a recipe that comes from Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish is the adjective for things belonging to Denmark.

clue.text: Could be mother and father split

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
rent, as a past participle of rend, means split or torn

explanation.surface: A mother and father may have separated.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'mother and father' as the definition; only 'Could be mother' defines, and 'father' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother is one example of a parent, hence the 'Could be'.

clue.text: Rickety sheep hobble

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
to hobble an animal is to shackle or fetter its legs

explanation.surface: A sheep with its legs tied is unsteady on its feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ramshackle is tumbledown and likely to collapse, like rickety furniture.

clue.text: See 1
Said you repaired car body out of stubbornness

indicators.note: repaired suggests the pieces are fixed up into a new arrangement
said signals that the word you is heard as the single letter it sounds like

parts.note: the word you is pronounced exactly like the letter U
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims they fixed a vehicle's bodywork out of sheer obstinacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' turns 'you' into U, and 'repaired' shuffles U with CARBODY.
explanation.definitionFit: Obduracy is obstinate refusal to change one's mind, the same as stubbornness.

clue.text: Story-teller getting duty list right managed to turn up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the whole string is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rota is a list of who is on duty when
ran, as in ran a business, means managed

explanation.surface: A storyteller is given a duty roster and manages to show up properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' reverses ROTA+R+RAN as a whole, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrator is the voice who tells a story.

clue.text: Bad manners of Rugby Union man holding up nurse

indicators.note: holding means the man's name contains the other piece

parts.note: Des is a short form of the man's name Desmond

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: SEN is State Enrolled Nurse, an old British nursing grade

explanation.surface: A rugby player behaves badly by propping up a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: SEN (State Enrolled Nurse) was a British nursing grade; Des is short for Desmond. In a down clue 'up' reverses, and 'holding' wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudeness is impolite behaviour, a lack of good manners.

clue.text: Symptom of dry nose disorder millions admitted

indicators.note: admitted means the letter is let into the middle of the jumble
disorder suggests the letters of dry nose are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A medical note on the symptom of a dry, disordered nose affecting millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' looks like part of the medical surface but is the anagram signal for DRY NOSE; 'admitted' puts M inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndrome is a recognised set of signs and complaints, loosely a symptom of an illness.

clue.text: Loved having a cheat looking angry

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or swindle them
red in the face, or seeing red, means angry

explanation.surface: A lover is cheated and left looking furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Adored means loved deeply, both as past tense verbs.

clue.text: Jack wants an evil French tea to drink!

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and so is an AB, an able-bodied seaman
a sin is an evil act
the is the French word for tea

explanation.surface: A man called Jack wants a wicked French cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: A JACK (or jack tar) is a sailor, as is an AB; French for tea is thé.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong aniseed spirit, something one might drink.

clue.text: Appoint Dora to run home

indicators.note: to run suggests the letters of the name Dora are set loose into a new order

parts.note: being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A girl named Dora is told to hurry home.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to appoint someone formally, especially to the priesthood.

clue.text: Refer satin dress to associate

indicators.note: dress, as in dressing a shop window, means the letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a satin outfit to a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' looks like a garment but is the anagram signal for REFER SATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To fraternise is to mix socially or keep company with others.

clue.text: Untidy people on board are anxious to boast

indicators.note: on, read with board, means the pieces are placed inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS, a steamship, is the crossword board one goes on
to care is to be worried or anxious
to crow is to boast

explanation.surface: Scruffy passengers aboard a ship worry about bragging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is a convention for being inside SS (a steamship).
explanation.definitionFit: Scarecrows are figures of rags in fields, so the word is used of anyone shabby-looking.

clue.text: Chaff makes you sick in time

parts.note: feeling bad means feeling sick
taken as written
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Something makes someone ill when they get it in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chaff' is not husks of grain here but the verb or noun for teasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful teasing banter, which is what chaff means as a noun.

clue.text: Thoughtful American backs workshop

indicators.note: backs means the American piece supports from behind, coming after the workshop

parts.note: an artist's studio is a workshop

explanation.surface: An American financier puts money behind a workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: A studious person is given to study and careful thought.

clue.text: Planning to reshape Meg's chin

indicators.note: to reshape indicates the letters of the phrase are formed into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A plan to give a woman called Meg plastic surgery on her chin.
explanation.definitionFit: Scheming means plotting, working out designs, often underhand ones.

clue.text: During chaotic trial copper scoffed, that's clear

indicators.note: during means the metal symbol sits within the jumbled trial
chaotic indicates the letters of trial are thrown into disorder

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to scoff food is to eat it greedily, so scoffed means ate

explanation.surface: A policeman eats during a messy court case, and that is plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's clear' reads as a closing remark, but 'clear' alone is the definition; 'During' and 'chaotic' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: Articulate speech is clear and distinct.

clue.text: Incentive get up if after tablet

indicators.note: in a down clue, get up means the combined letters are read upwards
after places the little word behind the tablet

parts.note: a pill is a tablet
taken as written

explanation.surface: An encouragement to rise if one has taken a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get up' looks like a phrase about rising from bed, but in a down clue it reverses the whole string, with 'after' fixing the order first.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a boost or stimulus, something that acts as an incentive.

clue.text: Talk about dropping last athletic event

indicators.note: dropping last means the final letter of the verb is lost

parts.note: to discuss something is to talk about it

explanation.surface: People talk about leaving out the final event of an athletics meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The discus is a field event in which a heavy disc is thrown.

clue.text: Shut up and wrote!

definitions.meaning: to pen animals is to shut them up in an enclosure
to pen a letter is to write it

explanation.definitionFit: Penned means both confined in a fold and written with a pen.

clue.text: In on the act, certainly

parts.note: taken as written
a deed is an act

explanation.surface: Someone is in on the plan, for sure.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an emphatic word of agreement, like truly or of course.

clue.text: Craftsman's endless cunning

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an artificer is a skilled craftsman; the 's reads as is

explanation.surface: A skilled worker's craftiness knows no bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Artifice is clever trickery, the noun sense of cunning.

clue.text: Handsome youth is following a college fellow

indicators.note: following places the word is after the other pieces

parts.note: a don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college

explanation.surface: A good-looking young man trails behind an academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, so the name stands for any handsome young man.

clue.text: Call in by shaking cooking pot

indicators.note: shaking means the letters of the phrase are jumbled up

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to drop by while shaking up the stew.
explanation.definitionFit: A billycan is a metal tin with a lid used by campers for boiling water or cooking.

clue.text: Officer some citizens ignore

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A junior officer whom some townspeople take no notice of.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a junior commissioned rank in navies and formerly in infantry regiments.

clue.text: Hated overlooking five spivs caught in action

indicators.note: caught in means the shortened word is held inside the act

parts.note: a deed is an action

indicators.note: overlooking means the five is left out of the word spivs

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Disliked spivs were nabbed in the middle of a scam.
explanation.walkthrough: A spiv is a British word for a flashy small-time crook; 'overlooking' drops the Roman five, and 'caught in' puts the rest inside the act.
explanation.definitionFit: Despised means looked down on and loathed.
